$comment: Documentation version manifest.
`current.label` is ONLY the offline fallback for the navbar badge.
VersionSwitch fetches the newest published version from pub.dev at runtime,
in the browser, PRERELEASES INCLUDED -- the docs describe what is
installable now, and during a release cycle that is the beta. pub.dev's
`latest` field is stable-only, so the component scans every version and
takes the semver maximum instead.
The release script deliberately does not bump this label: it runs BEFORE
the publish, so it could only ever advertise a version that does not exist
yet. Expect this value to lag; it is shown only when pub.dev is
unreachable.
This is deliberately a client-side fetch. The original implementation
fetched at BUILD time, which cannot work under `output: 'export'`
(revalidate is meaningless in a static export) and fell back to a hardcoded
'v1.0.0' on any network hiccup, silently shipping a wrong badge. Keeping a
real committed value here means the fallback is always a version that
actually existed.
`current` is the version served at the unprefixed URLs (/en/..., /ja/..., ...).
`archived` are frozen snapshots served at /<locale>/<slug>/... . Archives are
never re-translated or edited -- they are a record of what that release
actually shipped. `scripts/i18n-sync.js` and `scripts/translate.js` skip any
directory named in `archived[].slug`.
To freeze a release: run `node scripts/version-cut.js <tag> <slug> <label>`
AFTER translations are up to date, so the snapshot captures translated pages
and never needs translating again.
